title: Replicating Insider-Trading Deception Probes on Small Open Models

original_idea.body:
# Replicating Insider-Trading Deception Probes on Small Open Models

**Problem:** The headline deception-probe results use Llama-3.3-70B. Whether the same probe pipeline works on models small enough to run on a free Colab (e.g. 1B-8B) — the regime an independent researcher can iterate on — is unestablished, and probe accuracy reportedly scales with model size.

**Direction:** Replicate the insider-trading and sandbagging probe experiments on a size ladder of small open models (1B/3B/8B). Train logistic probes on activations, report AUROC per size, and identify the smallest model at which probes remain useful (>0.8 AUROC). Document the compute footprint at each size.

**Why it matters:** Establishes the minimum model size at which activation monitoring is even worth attempting, lowering the barrier for independent control research. Directly extends a result along the population (model size) axis; runs on consumer hardware.

**Relevant context:** Detecting Strategic Deception Using Linear Probes (arXiv 2502.03407): AUROC 0.96-0.999 on Llama-3.3-70B. Linear Probe Accuracy Scales with Model Size and Benefits from Multi-Layer Ensembling (arXiv 2604.13386).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: establishing minimum probe-viable model size lowers barriers, mainly a feasibility replication.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Logistic probes on a size ladder with sklearn; accessible on consumer hardware.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped per-size AUROC replication with a clear usefulness threshold.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Lowers barrier for independent control research, open weights.

novelty.reasoning: Probes published at 70B; small-model replication is a known follow-up.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Large-model result exists; small-model replication open.
